title: Secretary Rubio signs contract for U.S. participation in Expo 2030 Riyadh
excerpt: The agreement was signed by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Faisal bin Farhan in Atlanta, Georgia.
bodyHtml:
The United States State Department announced on October 30, 2026, that the United States will participate in Expo 2030 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Faisal bin Farhan signed the participation contract on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, Georgia.

According to the State Department, the United States will use Expo 2030 to showcase American innovation, expand commercial opportunities for U.S. businesses, and strengthen the bilateral relationship with Saudi Arabia. The department stated that the signing formalizes U.S. participation in the event.

Expo 2030 is scheduled to open in Riyadh on October 1, 2030, and will run through mid-March 2031. Saudi Arabia projects more than 42 million visitors from over 200 countries, which the State Department described as one of the decade’s largest public and commercial diplomacy platforms.

Formalizing participation is the first step in preparation and planning for the USA Pavilion at the event.
